youtube.title: What If You Had GTA 6 Money in Real Life? #Shorts
youtube.description:
What if you had GTA 6 money in real life? One heist, and you're a millionaire. Remy runs three tests on what a real million in cash is like.

Test 1, carrying it: a US banknote weighs about 1 gram. A million dollars in $100 bills is 10,000 bills, about 10 kg (22 lb), like a big bag of potatoes. Stacked up, the bills would stand about a meter tall.
Test 2, counting it: at one bill per second, 10,000 bills take 10,000 seconds, almost 3 hours (2.8 h).
Test 3, the bank: US banks have to report cash transactions over $10,000 to the government (a Currency Transaction Report), and splitting the cash into smaller deposits to dodge that report ("structuring") is a crime too.

So a million in cash isn't freedom. It's a heavy bag, a tired thumb, and a lot of paperwork. In the game, money is just a number. In real life, it weighs something. What would you do first with a real million?

Sources:
- A US banknote weighs about 1 gram, any denomination: U.S. Bureau of Engraving and Printing fun facts (archived): https://webarchive.library.unt.edu/web/20090114222615/http:/www.bep.treas.gov/document.cfm/18/106 , Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_one-hundred-dollar_bill
- Note thickness 0.0043 in (0.11 mm), so 10,000 notes are about 1.1 m: BEP / MoneyFactory (archived): https://webharvest.gov/peth04/20041015012917/http://www.moneyfactory.com/section.cfm/19
- Currency Transaction Report for cash over $10,000 in a business day (Bank Secrecy Act, 31 CFR 1010.311) and structuring is illegal (31 U.S.C. 5324): FinCEN: https://www.fincen.gov/sites/default/files/shared/CTRPamphlet.pdf , IRS: https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/bank-secrecy-act
- Counting time: 10,000 bills at 1 per second = 10,000 s = 2.8 hours (arithmetic). A 10 kg bag of potatoes is a common retail size (comparison only).

Not financial or legal advice.
Remy is fictional. Not affiliated with Rockstar Games or Take-Two. No game footage, art or logos are used. The cash shown is stylised (no real banknote images).
